subject: Re: Marconi, Great House Farm, Llandough
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Mathilde,

Thank you for your further reply and for carrying out the searches.

I appreciate your assistance, but I would like to clarify the scope and
conclusions of the search, as several points remain unresolved.

Firstly, I should correct one detail: the individual I am researching is *Mr
Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough near Penarth*, not "Mr William".
The surname is significant because family history suggests that my
great-grandfather, Mr Williams of Great House Farm, assisted Guglielmo
Marconi during the 1897 South Wales wireless experiments.

I fully understand that the absence of a result within the Postal Museum
catalogue does not necessarily mean that no such person or record existed.
However, I would be grateful if you could clarify the following:

   1. *Search methodology*

Could you confirm exactly which catalogue collections, series, or record
groups were searched for:

   - Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth)
   - Llandough
   - Lavernock
   - Marconi
   - wireless telegraphy demonstrations (1897)
   - GPO Telegraph Department
   - Engineering Department
   - Williams / Mr Williams


   2. *Scope of the negative result*

When you state that "nothing relevant came up", does this mean:

   - no indexed catalogue entries were found in Postal Museum collections;
   - no digitised records were found;
   - or that physical archival holdings were also checked?


   3. *Records relating to GPO personnel*

You mentioned that most Marconi and Telegraph Department records are held
at BT Archives. Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum holds any
catalogue references, finding aids, or transferred-record information
indicating where the relevant GPO engineering correspondence, reports,
notebooks, or staff records may have been moved?

   4. *The Williams connection*

The question I am trying to establish is not necessarily whether Mr
Williams was a Post Office employee. He may instead have been the
owner/occupier of Great House Farm who assisted Marconi locally.

Could you therefore confirm whether your search included references to:

   - private individuals assisting demonstrations;
   - hosts or local contacts connected with Marconi's experiments;
   - correspondence mentioning residents of Llandough, Penarth, or
   Lavernock?

I appreciate that the absence of a catalogue entry cannot prove that an
event or person did not exist, particularly where local residents or
private landowners were involved.

My aim is simply to establish the evidential trail: whether the Mr Williams
mentioned in contemporary accounts can be identified, and whether surviving
records connect him with Great House Farm and Marconi's experiments.

Thank you again for your assistance. I would be grateful for any further
clarification on the above points before I proceed to BT Archives and
Glamorgan Archives.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler

> Dear Mathilde,
>
> Thank you very much for taking the time to carry out these searches and
> for your detailed response.
>
> I appreciate the clarification regarding the distinction between Great
> House Farm, Llandough near Penarth and the similarly named location near
> Cowbridge. The Penarth/Llandough/Lavernock area is the location of interest.
>
> Your advice regarding BT Archives is very helpful, and I will follow this
> up with them, as the surviving GPO Telegraph and wireless records appear
> likely to be held there.
>
> I am also grateful for the information about the Post Office family
> history records. My main interest is not that Mr Williams was necessarily a
> Post Office employee, but whether the individual mentioned in contemporary
> accounts as assisting Marconi at Great House Farm can be identified. Family
> history passed down through my great grandfather's line suggests that a Mr
> Williams of Great House Farm assisted Marconi during his South Wales
> experiments, and I am trying to establish whether this can be connected to
> my ancestor.
>
> If possible, could you let me know whether the search you carried out
> included any of the following terms or collections, as this may help me
> understand the scope of the search:
>
>    - Great House Farm (Llandough/Penarth)
>    - Llandough
>    - Lavernock
>    - Marconi
>    - wireless telegraphy demonstrations (1897)
>    - GPO Telegraph Department / Engineering Department
>
> I will also contact Glamorgan Archives, as you suggest, since local
> newspapers, estate records, or correspondence may contain information not
> held in the national collections.
>
> Thank you again for your assistance. Your guidance has helped narrow down
> where the relevant evidence is most likely to survive.
>
> Kind regards,
>
> Sion Buckler
>
>
>
> On Wed, 29 Jul 2026, 07:31 Archives, <[email redacted]> wrote:
>
> Dear Sion,
>
>
>
> Thank you for your enquiry. I will do my best to check if we have
> surviving records of this demonstration, although most of the records about
> telecommunications were transferred to BT Archives so they might have more
> information than us: https://www.bt.com/about/bt/our-history/bt-archives
>
>    - Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth, Cardiff (not Great House
>    Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge)
>
> I couldn’t find any record mentioning Great House Farm, Llandough. For
> Penarth, there were some results but they were all dated much later than
> the demonstration. We have many records on Cardiff, which you can find on
> our online catalogue Here, but nothing relevant seemed to have come up.
>
>    - Llandough, Penarth, Lavernock and the surrounding wireless
>    demonstration sites.
>
> Nothing came up for Lavernock either, the locations are too precise for
> this type of records to have reached our archives. I searched for ‘wireless
> demonstration’ and POST 88 Series titled ‘Post Office: Wireless Telegraphy
> and Telephony’ mentions such events, but all the files are kept in BT
> Archives.
>
>    - Guglielmo Marconi's 1897 demonstrations.
>
> Almost all the files related to Marconi are held in BT Archives.
>
>    - GPO Telegraph or Engineering Department records concerning these
>    demonstrations.
>
> See above.
>
>    - Correspondence, reports, notebooks, diaries, staff lists, expense
>    claims, photographs or plans relating to engineers or officials present.
>
> See above.
>
>    - Any references to Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, who
>    family history suggests assisted Marconi before, during or after his stay
>    at the property.
>
> I couldn’t find any specific file about a Mr William from Great House
> Farm, but the main records we have that are useful for family history
> research are the Appointment Books, and the pension and gratuity records.
> We also have Establishment Books and staff magazines that can be helpful
> too. You can find more information about what we hold here:
> https://www.postalmuseum.org/collections/the-archive/family-history/
>  Please bear in mind that most villages, small towns, hamlets, etc. such as
> Llandough had business that ran a postal service, and these people were not
> directly employed by the Post Office, therefore, we won’t have any
> information. If Mr Williams had another business, he was likely not
> employed by the Post Office. A local archive might hold newspaper cuttings
> or other information about this person: https://glamarchives.gov.uk/
>
> You are welcome to visit our archives, but I believe most of the records
> and information you are looking for will be held at BT Archives. You can
> contact them directly to organise an appointment.
>
>
>
> I hope this helps,
>
>
>
> Best regards,
>
>
>
> Mathilde

> Dear Archive Team,
>
> I am conducting historical research into the General Post Office's
> involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's wireless demonstrations in South Wales
> during 1897.
>
> Post Office Ltd has advised that your archive is the most likely
> repository for surviving historic GPO records relating to this period.
>
> I would be grateful if you could search for any records relating to:
>
>    - Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth, Cardiff (not Great House
>    Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge).
>    - Llandough, Penarth, Lavernock and the surrounding wireless
>    demonstration sites.
>    - Guglielmo Marconi's 1897 demonstrations.
>    - GPO Telegraph or Engineering Department records concerning these
>    demonstrations.
>    - Correspondence, reports, notebooks, diaries, staff lists, expense
>    claims, photographs or plans relating to engineers or officials present.
>    - Any references to Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, who
>    family history suggests assisted Marconi before, during or after his stay
>    at the property.
>
> If records relating specifically to Mr Williams cannot be located, I would
> also appreciate details of any records identifying GPO personnel, visitors
> or local residents connected with the demonstrations, as these may help
> establish the historical context.
>
> If another archive holds any of these records, I would be grateful if you
> could advise where I should direct my enquiry.
>
> Mr Williams of Great House Farm was my great grandad. I am trying to
> ascertain if the Mr Williams post office worker, mentioned helping Marconi
> in the article, was the same man as my great grandfather. I am also looking
> for any more connections between my family, my former home and Marconi and
> the radio experiments at lavernock point. Which I understand were already
> underway before Marconi arrived to South Wales.
>
> Thank you for your time and assistance. I look forward to your response.
>
> Kind regards,
>
>
>
> Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sgt)
>
> Royal Signals Cyber & Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
